The test image shows two bell peppers with large, dark sunken lesions covering much of the fruit surface. Key features:
- Large, dark brown/black sunken lesions
- Concentric ring pattern visible within lesions
- Shiny/wet appearance
- Affects fruit surface broadly

Top candidates: **Anthracnose** (sunken dark lesions with concentric rings on fruit), **Rhizopus_Soft_Rots** (soft rot on fruit), **Gray_Mold** (fungal fruit rot).

Now viewing one reference from each top candidate class:

The Anthracnose Bugwood_16 reference is a near-perfect match to the test image — same yellow/orange bell pepper, same large dark black sunken lesion covering the fruit, same concentric pattern. The Bugwood IDs are even consecutive (1568069 vs 1568070), confirming they're from the same source.

**Summary:**
- Test image: two bell peppers with large, dark sunken lesions, concentric rings, wet/shiny surface
- Anthracnose reference (Bugwood_16): identical presentation — bell pepper, large black sunken anthracnose lesion
- Rhizopus_Soft_Rots: whole wilted plant (not matching)
- Gray_Mold: microscopy image (not matching)
